subject: Choosing cabinet finishes and handles
hook: Is an oak-effect kitchen the same as real oak?
fb:
A fair question we get asked at consultations: is an oak-effect kitchen the same as real oak?

No, and we think you should know exactly what you are buying. Our oak-effect doors are a woodgrain finish on engineered board, with matching ABS edging. What that gives you is the warm look of oak, the same colour on every door across the run, a surface you simply wipe down, and nothing to oil or re-seal.

We never describe it as solid oak, because it is not.

Got another question about finishes? Ask away, or book a free consultation:

gbp:
Is an oak-effect kitchen the same as real oak?

No. Our oak-effect finishes are a woodgrain finish applied to engineered board, edged with matching ABS edging. We will always describe them accurately.

What oak-effect gives you is the warmth and grain of oak with a consistent colour across every door, a wipe-clean surface for everyday cooking, and no oiling or re-sealing. It sits well alongside charcoal, matt white and black woodgrain finishes, and with antique gold or matt black handles.

We help you compare real samples in your own kitchen at a free, no-obligation design consultation, followed by an itemised quote. Every kitchen is manufactured in our own Hanley workshop in Stoke-on-Trent and installed by our own team.
